posts.text:
As a mom of two teenagers, I don’t have to ask parents about raising kids in a digital world—I’m living it.

For far too long, Big Tech has chosen profits over protecting our children. Congress cannot continue to sit on the sidelines, doing nothing is not an option.
posts.summary: Demands Congress regulate Big Tech to protect children from social media harms
posts.quote:
As a mom of two teenagers, I don’t have to ask parents about raising kids in a digital world—I’m living it.

For far too long, Big Tech has chosen profits over protecting our children. Congress cannot continue to sit on the sidelines, doing nothing is not an option.

posts.text:
Thrilled to see Senate Commerce take action today by advancing the Kids Online Safety Act championed by my good friend, @MarshaBlackburn. 

Parents and children have waited long enough on Congress—this generational crisis demands action and Big Tech must be held accountable. Let’s get this to the Senate floor and to @POTUS now.

The youth mental health crisis is crippling our nation, and the rise of social media is fueling it.

The Stop the Scroll Act, which @SenFettermanPA and I introduced, would require mental health warning labels on social media platforms, just as cigarette packs have warnings. Our bill goes a step further by requiring those labels to point users to mental health resources.
